Contextual English gloss: voice produced with less apparent forcing
Note: Perceived/inferred reduction in forcing or tension; no direct physiological measurement is implied.

Contextual English gloss: less throaty or constricted, more open-sounding voice
Note: Pedagogical contrast to a throaty/constricted sound; not an anatomical definition of an 'open throat'.

Contextual English gloss: softer, more supple vocal quality
Note: A perceptual/timbral descriptor; 'soft' here does not simply mean lower loudness.

Contextual English gloss: less breathy, with reduced audible air leakage
Note: Perceptual breathiness; not a direct measurement of airflow or glottal closure.

Contextual English gloss: production perceived as involving a lower laryngeal setting
Note: Internal laryngeal action is perceived/inferred, not directly measured.

Contextual English gloss: sound consistent with firmer vocal-fold closure and a stronger, fuller tone
Note: Vocal-fold closure is inferred from the sound; it was not directly observed or measured.

Contextual English gloss: more adequate and released mouth opening
Note: The adequacy of mouth opening is perceived/inferred in the pedagogical context; it was not quantified.

Contextual English gloss: more accurate intonation
Note: Refers to perceived improvement in pitch accuracy.

Contextual English gloss: more natural, well-formed vibrato
Note: Perceptual evaluation of vibrato quality; not an operational definition of a vibrato metric.

Contextual English gloss: more appropriate vowel placement and articulation
Note: 'Position' is a pedagogical/articulatory concept, not a fixed anatomical coordinate.

Contextual English gloss: greater awareness or sensation of resonance
Note: A pedagogical sensation/awareness of resonance; not a direct measurement of resonating cavities.

Contextual English gloss: more resonant vocal quality
Note: Perceptual resonance quality; not defined by a single acoustic variable.

Contextual English gloss: production perceived as involving a raised soft palate
Note: Soft-palate action is perceived/inferred, not directly measured.

Contextual English gloss: greater vocal fullness or apparent volume
Note: 'Voluminoso' can imply fullness as well as apparent volume; no calibrated SPL measurement is implied.

Contextual English gloss: less inward or muffled, more open-sounding voice
Note: A pedagogical/perceptual description of reduced inward or muffled quality.

Contextual English gloss: resonance perceived at a higher position
Note: Resonance 'position' is a pedagogical percept or image, not a literal anatomical location.

Contextual English gloss: more forward, 'in-the-mask' resonance
Note: Traditional bel canto term retained; the gloss indicates a perceived forward resonance, not a literal anatomical site.

Contextual English gloss: voice with greater carrying power or projection
Note: Perceived projection/carrying quality; it was not measured at a physical distance.

Contextual English gloss: brighter vocal timbre
Note: Perceptual brightness; not equated a priori with spectral centroid or any single acoustic measure.

Contextual English gloss: greater depth and richness of vocal timbre
Note: Perceptual timbral depth; not equated with lower pitch or a single spectral measure.

Contextual English gloss: less nasal vocal quality
Note: Perceptual nasality; no nasalance measurement is implied.

Contextual English gloss: more unified and consistent resonance across the five vowels
Note: Pedagogical consistency across vowels; does not imply that the vowels become acoustically identical.

Contextual English gloss: breathing perceived as more effectively costo-diaphragmatic
Note: Respiratory action is perceived/inferred; no direct respiratory measurement is implied.

Contextual English gloss: voice carried on a well-coordinated breath flow
Note: Traditional bel canto term retained; this is a contextual gloss of voice-breath coordination, not a literal or operational definition.

Contextual English gloss: better control and management of the breath
Note: Functional/pedagogical breath control; not a direct airflow measurement.

Contextual English gloss: more stable appoggio and breath-support coordination
Note: Traditional bel canto term retained; the gloss does not reduce appoggio to a single physiological mechanism.

Contextual English gloss: more continuous and well-coordinated breath flow
Note: Perceived/functional breath flow; not a direct airflow measurement.
